name: Beerah
overview: Beerah was a male leader from the tribe of Reuben, noted in Scripture as the son of Baal. He is uniquely identified as a leader of the Reubenites who was carried away into exile by Tilgath-pilneser. This historical detail highlights his role during a period of captivity and displacement.
namesAndTitles: The name Beerah means "cistern" or "well," reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it carries a meaning associated with a source of water or provision.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Beerah was the son of Baal. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Beerah's significance lies in his leadership among the Reubenites during a time of exile, as he was taken captive by the Assyrian king Tilgath-pilneser. His mention underscores the historical reality of Israelite tribes facing judgment and captivity. This event serves as a reminder of God's dealings with His people and the consequences of their actions.
